transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello — do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You can go back to light exercise after 1 week, and that includes gardening. Try to keep it light at first.  

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great to know, thank you. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
If you were using eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it’s safe to continue using them unless you’ve been told otherwise.  

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Alright, thanks for clarifying. I'm also very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It can be normal for the eyes to be a bit sensitive to light while they adjust to the new lenses. If it’s mild and things just seem brighter than usual, wear sunglasses when you go outside.  

But significant pain when it’s bright, or severe light sensitivity, is not normal, especially if the eye is also red and painful.  

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That makes sense, thanks for the advice. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It’s common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation. It should improve quickly and settle down over time. If it’s still blurry, or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it.  

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all my questions for now. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have all your questions been answered?

verdict.label: pass
